Show HN: Dedoomify – AI news, minus the doom
item.description:
What if AI failures were described like ordinary software issues? Paste a link to an AI article and dedoomify turns down the apocalypse: "the model is misaligned" becomes "the model has a bug".

Less Skynet. More software. And every change is highlighted with the original text one hover or tap away. You can try an example without signing up or installing anything!

The default engine runs on quick phrase rules or you can run a local AI model in your browser via WebGPU; there's also a Chrome extension that applies the rules to the page you’re reading. And all the code is open source! https://github.com/akspad/dedoomify

There's so much AI doom in the world right now that I wanted to see what articles would look like reframed to be less doom and gloom and instead more matter-of-fact (sprinkled with some sunshine and roses).

Let me know what you think - suggestions and improvements are always welcome :)

Ask HN: Which AI Security tool do you use and why for your repositories?
item.description:
Hello World!

So I am new to the world of cybersecurity, and after some back and forth with AI, I chose to use a specific tool that was recommended for automated vulnerability detection & patching, but I think the issue I encountered is something common to all similar platforms that provide AI security fixes in 2026.

It proposed a fix to an issue labeled 'critical'. I gave the specific file and the fix to Gemini, and, it disagreed strongly.

My trust in the platform immediately degraded.

It shows in my thinking that AI security platforms for repositories are unreliable, unless you cross check every critical/high vulnerability as a human with another AI tool as well. For example, for another issue labeled 'High', the fix, I cross-checked, was correct in that case.

But that that one 'critical' issue, which turned out to be not a bug at all, and certainly not critical at all, has degraded my trust strongly in AI security platforms for automated vulnerability detection & patching. Note, to prevent confusion, with automated patching I mean automated pull requests with AI-proposed fixes, pending explicit human merging.

Now, I wonder what you guys use (instead, if at all), and how reliable your security tool(s) are, if at all, for automated vulnerability detection (& patching.)

Happy Coding!

Worldwide Wishes,

Behan

Show HN: Airlock, which sandboxes AI agents, is available on the Mac App Store
item.description:
Now that Airlock is available on the Mac App Store, I thought it was worth a resubmission. Quickly run your AI agents (Claude, Codex) in a disposable VM. Block the agent from making requests to unknown or untrusted hosts, and get a log of everything that it does - then only bring back the changes you actually want.

It's free, and has no tracking or analytics. It requires a Mac with Apple silicon running macOS 26+

Recruiters told me AI screening overlooks the best candidates. True?
item.description:
After submitting a lot of CVs recently, I’ve separately been asking recruiters and hiring managers, in-house and agency, how they’re coping now that applications can be written, enhanced or fabricated by AI, and graded by AI.

An in-house recruiter at a 2,000-person company said their ranking tool grades CVs A to D, and the people they end up hiring are frequently the C’s. An agency director trialled fully automated screeners and said they “overlooked some of the strongest candidates”. A hiring manager, after a run of fabricated applications, built their own grader and auto-rejects anyone who matches the job spec too closely, on the basis that no real candidate meets 100% of the requirements. I’ve seen a few similar posts along the lines of “I’d probably be rejected applying for my own job”. Everyone said most CVs now have AI involvement, many are the job spec fed back as experience, and the truth only comes out on the screening call.

If you hire engineers or any other role: has the CV stopped carrying signal for you, and what are you using instead? If AI screening is actually working for you, which tool and how? I’d like the counter-examples as much as the confirmations.
